records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1`** — `{{#unless automatic}}` is evaluated inside the `group-member` item view, whose context is the individual `member` (a `User`), not the parent `Group`. `User` records have no `automatic` attribute, so this always resolves falsy and the "remove" (×) icon is shown on **every** member row, including members of automatic groups — exactly the case this PR is supposed to handle correctly. The backend still rejects the removal (422 in `add_members`/`remove_member`, `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:69,88`), but `Discourse.Group#removeMember` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-49`) has no `.catch`, so the admin gets silent failure with no feedback. Fix: gate the remove link on the parent group's `automatic` flag (e.g. pass it into the item view, or check `controller.automatic`/a bound property), and add error handling to `removeMember`.
records.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, members are rendered as `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so the `group-member` view/template context is the individual `member` (a `Discourse.User`). records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:21`** — `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. Ember's `{{each}}` "item form" in this era exposes item-view wiring via `itemViewClass`, not `itemView`; using an unrecognized hash option is likely to silently no-op, meaning the member list may not render at all via the custom item view. This should be manually verified by loading the admin group page; if confirmed, rename to `itemViewClass="group-member"`.

**`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`** — `group.users.delete(user_id)` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if `user_id` doesn't belong to the group's current membership (e.g., double-click, stale UI, already-removed member) — Rails resolves bare ids via `find` before deleting. There's no rescue, so this becomes an unhandled 500 for what should be a benign/idempotent operation. Wrap in a rescue (or check membership first) and return a normal success/404 instead of blowing up.

**Test coverage gap** — There is no spec at all for `GroupsController#members` (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`), even though this PR's core fix (removing the automatic-group-only pagination limitation, returning the new `{members, meta}` shape) lives there. This is the most behaviorally significant change in the diff and ships with zero test coverage.
records.rationale: The diff makes a behaviorally significant change in `GroupsController#members` (now always paginates, and returns a new JSON shape `{ members, meta }` instead of `render_serialized(...)`). If `group.save` fails for unrelated reasons, the response reports an error even though the membership change already took effect — misleading success/failure semantics. Consider dropping the redundant `save` or reloading/checking membership state directly.

records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22`** — no upper bound on `params[:limit]`; a client can request an arbitrarily large page size. Consider clamping (e.g. `[limit, 200].min`).
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum clamp. This allows a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit`, which can cause excessive DB load/memory usage (performance/DoS risk).
